deposit_profile: A deposit address is one customer's: everything it sends goes to the wallets of one exchange (a sweep into a hot wallet), few outside addresses ever pay it, it never swaps on a DEX, and it is no token, pool, router or smart account.
hint: Answer: write every address in full (0x plus 40 characters), also when it repeats one named earlier and also when the user asks for shorter ones (name them instead); a transfer moves tokens, so write "tokens worth about N USD", never "sent N USD" or a $ figure; never draw the flows in text, ASCII or Mermaid, the host draws them. 0x2f6c24fcace697f8f52d14c94a57e9eb1e2666a1 carries no deposit mark: no SWEPT link and no exchange_role. Say that the graph shows no sweep of it into a listed exchange hot wallet. That is not proof the address belongs to no exchange; its labels and its links say what else it is. Its behaviour, as the graph counts it: 214 addresses paid it (1 of them exchange wallets), it paid 57 addresses (1 of them exchange wallets), it swapped on 291 DEX pools, it approved 11 spenders. What a deposit address does not do, and this one did: it swapped on 291 DEX pools; it paid 56 addresses that are no exchange wallet. Give these facts as the reason and no other: set no threshold of your own for payers, volume or sweeps. Asked how a deposit address behaves, what makes an address one or what rules one out, answer with deposit_profile.
